name: Lethal Infantile Mitochondrial Myopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Infantile Mitochondrial Myopathy

criteria.description: Onset of severe hypotonia and muscle weakness within the first year of life
Elevated lactate and pyruvate levels in blood and/or cerebrospinal fluid
Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities including ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
Identification of pathogenic mutations in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial function
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia involvement or cerebral atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (clinical presentation, biochemical evidence, and muscle biopsy findings) with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and for family counseling.

searchTerms: very high lactic acid in blood

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate)
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions or cerebral atrophy
Muscle MRI demonstrating muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in mitochondrial DNA (e.g., MT-ATP6, MT-ND genes)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficiency
Electron microscopy showing abnormal mitochondrial morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle biopsy
Muscle biopsy showing structural myopathic changes without mitochondrial defects

redFlags: Rapidly progressive hypotonia and muscle weakness in infancy
Persistent lactic acidosis despite supportive care
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Parikh S, Goldstein A, Karaa A, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015 Sep;17(9):689-701.
